knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian Determinant of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}3 \left(2 u + v\right)^{3} \\ 3 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{3}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=3 \left(2 u + v\right)^{3}$ and $y=3 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{3}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=18 \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=9 \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=18 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 18 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}18 \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}&9 \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}\\18 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}&- 18 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(18 \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(- 18 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(9 \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(18 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\\&=- 1944 \left(u - v\right)^{2} \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian Determinant of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}3 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{3} \\ 3 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=3 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{3}$ and $y=3 \left(u - v\right)^{2}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=9 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=18 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=6 u - 6 v\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 6 u + 6 v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}9 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}&18 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\\6 u - 6 v&- 6 u + 6 v\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(9 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(- 6 u + 6 v\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(18 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(6 u - 6 v\right)\\&=\left(- 162 u + 162 v\right) \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}\left(u + 2 v\right)^{3} \\ 2 \left(u - v\right)^{3}\end{bmatrix}.

$$

Here, we have $x=\left(u + 2 v\right)^{3}$ and $y=2 \left(u - v\right)^{3}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=3 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=6 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}3 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}&6 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\\6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}&- 6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(3 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(- 6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(6 \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(6 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\right)\\&=- 54 \left(u - v\right)^{2} \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
